screening_decisions.reason: RCT evaluating nitroprusside gel vs placebo for IUD insertion pain in nulliparous women. Primary outcome is subject-reported pain with IUD insertion measured by VAS. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT evaluating ibuprofen 800mg vs placebo for IUD insertion pain. Pain measured using 100-mm VAS immediately following IUD insertion. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT evaluating bladder distension (full vs empty bladder) as intervention for IUC insertion. Women's pain scores measured and compared between groups. Non-pharmacological intervention for IUC insertion pain meets criteria.

RCT evaluating intracervical lidocaine injection vs NSAID for LNG-IUS insertion pain in nulliparous women. Pain measured immediately after insertion and at 2h and 6h using VAS and facial pain scale. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT evaluating ibuprofen 800mg vs placebo for LNG-IUS insertion pain. Pain measured with tenaculum placement and with insertion using numeric scales. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT evaluating vaginal misoprostol vs placebo for IUD insertion pain. Pain measured as secondary outcome. Includes both copper and LNG-IUDs, nulli- and multiparous women. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT evaluating buccal misoprostol vs placebo for IUD insertion pain in nulliparous women. Pain measured at multiple time points including tenaculum placement, IUD insertion, and 5 min post-insertion using 100-mm VAS. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT evaluating sublingual misoprostol vs placebo for repeat LNG-IUS insertion. Pain at insertion measured (no or mild pain reported). Meets all selection criteria for RCT evaluating intervention for IUC insertion pain.
RCT evaluating ibuprofen 400mg vs placebo for copper IUD insertion pain in first-time users. Pain measured immediately after insertion using 10-cm VAS. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT evaluating sublingual misoprostol+diclofenac vs diclofenac alone for IUD insertion in women with no previous vaginal delivery. Objective includes investigating pain reduction. Meets selection criteria for RCT evaluating intervention for IUC insertion pain.
RCT evaluating ibuprofen 600mg vs placebo for IUD insertion pain. Pain assessed during insertion, first 4-6 hours, and following days using 10-point NRS. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT comparing oral tramadol vs naproxen vs placebo for IUD insertion pain. Pain measured using VAS (0-10) after insertion. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT evaluating buccal misoprostol vs placebo for IUD insertion pain in nulliparous women. Pain measured before and after IUD insertion using 100-mm VAS. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT evaluating intracervical 2% lidocaine gel vs placebo for IUD insertion pain. Pain measured at four time points using 100-mm VAS. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT evaluating vaginal nitroglycerin gel vs placebo for IUD insertion pain in nulliparous women. Primary outcome is subject-reported pain with IUD passage through cervix measured by 100-mm VAS. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT evaluating 1% lidocaine paracervical block vs no anesthetic for IUD insertion pain. Pain measured at multiple points including tenaculum placement, IUD insertion, and 5 min post-procedure using 100-mm VAS. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT evaluating lidocaine 2% gel vs lubricant gel vs no intervention for copper IUD insertion pain. Pain measured immediately after insertion using 0-10 cm VAS. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT evaluating intrauterine lidocaine infusion vs normal saline for IUD insertion pain. Pain measured at tenaculum placement and during IUD insertion using 0-9 point scale. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT evaluating sublingual misoprostol+diclofenac vs diclofenac alone for IUD insertion in nulliparous women. Pain estimated on VAS (1-10) at insertion. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT evaluating vaginal misoprostol vs placebo for IUD insertion pain in nulligravidas. Moderate-to-severe pain at IUD insertion measured as outcome. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT evaluating lavender inhalation vs placebo for IUD insertion pain and anxiety. Pain measured immediately after insertion using VAS (0-10). Meets selection criteria for RCT evaluating intervention for IUC insertion pain.

RCT evaluating self-administered misoprostol vs placebo for IUD insertion pain in nulliparous women. Pain measured before insertion, immediately post-insertion, and before discharge using VAS. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT evaluating novel topical lidocaine formulation vs placebo for IUD insertion pain. Pain measured using VAS during first 10 minutes after insertion and at 30 minutes. Meets all selection criteria.

RCT evaluating paracervical block with 1% lidocaine vs placebo vs no treatment for IUD insertion pain. Pain measured at tenaculum placement, IUD insertion, and 5 minutes after procedure using visual pain scale. Meets all selection criteria.
RCT evaluating misoprostol vs placebo for IUD insertion pain in nulliparous women. Primary outcome is pain at time of insertion using 100-mm VAS. Meets all selection criteria.

This is an RCT evaluating self-administered lidocaine gel vs placebo for reducing IUD insertion pain in nulliparous women. Pain outcomes were measured using VAS at multiple time points including tenaculum placement and during insertion. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a descriptive article/report of author's experience with intracervical block for IUD insertion since 1975. Not an RCT - no randomization, no control group, no comparative data.

This is a prospective cohort study comparing pain between women with and without vaginal delivery history. Not an RCT - no intervention being tested, merely observational comparison of pain based on parity.
This is a qualitative study exploring women's perceptions and barriers to IUD use. Not an RCT, does not evaluate any intervention for pain reduction during IUD insertion.
This is a review article providing practical advice and consensus recommendations for pain management during IUC insertion. Not an RCT.
This is a methodological article about GRADE guidelines for rating quality of evidence. Not related to IUD insertion pain interventions.
This is a committee opinion/clinical practice guideline about LARC methods for adolescents. Not an RCT evaluating pain interventions.
This is a review article that critically evaluates evidence for pain management strategies during IUC insertion. While it includes RCTs, this is a review, not an original RCT.
This is a review article about misoprostol use in gynecology, covering various indications including abortion and hysteroscopy. Not an RCT specifically evaluating misoprostol for IUD insertion pain.
This appears to be an observational study evaluating actual vs expected pain levels with a specific insertion technique. Not an RCT comparing an intervention to control/placebo for pain reduction.
This is a methodological article about GRADE guidelines for systematic reviews. Not related to IUD insertion pain interventions.
This is explicitly a nonrandomized study assessing predictors of difficult/painful IUD insertion. Not an RCT evaluating an intervention for pain reduction.
This appears to be a brief article/commentary noting lack of guidelines for pain management during IUD insertion. Not an RCT.

This is a systematic review of intrauterine local anesthesia for various gynecologic procedures. While it includes RCTs, this is a review article, not an original RCT. Also states evidence was insufficient for IUD insertion specifically.
This is an observational study using questionnaires to explore women's use of oral analgesia before IUD fitting. Not an RCT - women chose whether to take analgesia, no randomization.
This is a technical report about contraception for adolescents, covering various aspects of contraceptive use. Not an RCT evaluating pain interventions.
This is a meta-analysis of RCTs evaluating analgesics for IUD placement. While it analyzes RCTs, this is a meta-analysis, not an original RCT.
This is an RCT but it evaluates nitric oxide donors for cervical ripening before surgical termination of pregnancy (abortion), not for IUD insertion pain. Wrong population and procedure.
This is a survey/questionnaire study describing practice patterns among doctors regarding IUD insertion techniques. Not an RCT evaluating an intervention.
This is a methodology paper describing the process of developing a prospective meta-analysis collaboration. Not an RCT with results.
This is a review article discussing evidence for misoprostol use prior to IUD insertion. Not an original RCT.

This is a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial evaluating meptazinol for pain relief following IUD insertion. Pain outcomes were assessed. Meets selection criteria as an RCT evaluating an intervention for IUD insertion pain.

This is described as a clinical trial where women were randomly recruited into lavender, placebo, and control groups. Pain was measured using VAS after IUD insertion. Appears to be an RCT evaluating an intervention for IUD insertion pain.
This appears to be a technique description article about a simplified paracervical block approach. Not an RCT - no comparative data or randomization mentioned.

This is a Cochrane review summarizing RCTs of NSAIDs for bleeding or pain associated with IUD use. While it mentions trials of prophylactic use around insertion, this is a review, not an original RCT.
